messages:
Nina: Quick heads-up — I'm kicking off a Q3 initiative around 'autoscale safety zones' for Dedicated. Goal: let customers have burst capacity without risking noisy-neighbor SLO blasts. Want initial feedback on scope and launch criteria.

Raj: 100% agree. Need clear eviction priority lanes + a fast throttle path.

Lex: Tie safety zones to SLA tiers. e.g., gold zones have stricter non-preemptable thresholds. Risk: if we keep too much reserved, cost goes up.

Marta: From sales: multiple customers asked for guaranteed burst for sale events. They'll pay for committed burst blocks, but expect simple UX.

Sam: Implementation thought: per-customer token bucket (safetyBudget) that is consumed during bursts, with cooldown windows. Backend: fast checks in the runtime.

Nina: Good. For rollout and launch criteria I propose: 1) dogfood on internal stacks, 2) beta with 2–3 customers, 3) GA. Success metrics: P95 latency under 300ms for gold under typical load, zero SLO breaches for gold during normal ops, and token exhaustion events < 0.5% of minutes.

Raj: Need feature flag + telemetry. Also add an emergency eviction metric: percent of requests evicted vs served.

Lex: Ops requirements: fallback policies — if burst fails, route to cheaper compatible model or degrade gracefully. Must have alerting when safetyBudget drained for > 5m.

Marta: Pricing note: propose a "reserved-burst" SKU: monthly base + per-token overage. Customers want predictable ceilings.

Amy: CS asks for a config template and runbook: how to set burst windows, TTLs, and testing guidance.

Raj: Quick config sketch we can prototype in the runtime (pseudo-yaml):
```
autoscale:
  safety_zones:
    - name: gold
      min_capacity: 80
      preemptable: false
    - name: standard
      min_capacity: 30
      preemptable: true
  burst_policy:
    token_bucket:
      capacity: 5000
      refill_rate: 100
      cooldown_secs: 3600
```

Sam: Perf note: token checks must be O(1) in hot path. Options: in-runtime sharded counters or Redis with a LUA atomic script. Sharding reduces cross-pool contention.

Nina: Owners: @Raj, @Sam, @Lex. Deliverables for next sync: spec doc (including pricing options), rollout plan, telemetry dashboard mocks. Sync Fri 9am PT — can everyone make it?

Raj: can do.

Sam: ok for me.

Lex: ok :thumbsup:

Marta: I can join the beta convo with two accounts we flagged.

Amy: I'll draft the CS runbook skeleton by EOD Thursday.

deploy-bot: feature-flag created: feature.autoscale_safety_zones -> OFF

Nina: thanks all — I'll drop a short spec link before the sync.
